ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Epithelial adaptation to chronic irritation

A smoker has a bronchial biopsy in which ciliated columnar epithelium has been replaced by stratified squamous epithelium without invasion. Which interpretation best explains the change and its immediate functional tradeoff in this patient?

  1. Metaplasia with reduced mucociliary protection
  2. Hypertrophy with enhanced ciliary clearance
  3. Hyperplasia with preservation of all original functions
  4. Anaplasia proving invasive carcinoma
  5. Liquefactive necrosis with complete tissue dissolution
Answer and explanation

Metaplasia with reduced mucociliary protection

Squamous replacement may tolerate irritation but loses specialized ciliary clearance.

Option explanations

Metaplasia with reduced mucociliary protection: Squamous replacement may tolerate irritation but loses specialized ciliary clearance.

Hypertrophy with enhanced ciliary clearance: The differentiated cell type has changed, not merely its size.

Hyperplasia with preservation of all original functions: The new epithelium does not preserve normal mucociliary function.

Anaplasia proving invasive carcinoma: Metaplasia without invasion does not establish carcinoma.

Liquefactive necrosis with complete tissue dissolution: The epithelium is viable and organized rather than liquefied.
